Lee: diagnosis with a short-route preference · expanded view

Lee is fascinated by differential diagnosis and explains case stories from a school health club. Lee currently hopes to start earning quickly and chooses dental assisting preparation, despite preferring physician responsibilities in the role questions. These are two real preferences to discuss rather than proof the routes are interchangeable. Lee wants an expensive future lifestyle before understanding its training timeline.

Narrative model, with its answers frozen before the first run. Optional questions omitted by the shorter route are marked. These are synthetic checks, not observations of students.

Authored model & first-run review

Health-club reading and family conversations; no clinical performance experience. The short route reflects current money concerns, not inability to study.

The model is a route-conflict check. Neither an expensive goal nor an education preference is an aptitude score.

Choice screens: 97 including lifestyle and profession questions; introductory screens are not counted.

Low experience does not change interests or career rankings · A more expensive lifestyle changes money needs, not interest matching · Answers and recommendations survive save/reload · Open profiles do not force three pathways or a profession · Optional detail preserves all six official interest scores

1. Lifestyle questions & answers

  1. Where would you feel at home?

    Answer: Room to spread out — A larger apartment or rental home.

    • Share a place — A room of your own. Shared living space.
    • A small place — A modest apartment with the basics.
    • My own space — A comfortable one-bedroom apartment.
    • ✓ Room to spread out — A larger apartment or rental home. (selected)
    • A standout home — A high-end home with extra space and comforts.
  2. How would you like to get around?

    Answer: A premium car — A car that is part of the experience.

    • Keep it light — Walking, cycling, transit, and occasional rides.
    • A car I own — No loan payment. Include upkeep and a replacement fund.
    • A reliable used car — A compact car for everyday trips.
    • A newer car — More comfort and newer features.
    • ✓ A premium car — A car that is part of the experience. (selected)
  3. What is your food-at-home style?

    Answer: Food I love — Specialty ingredients and more convenience.

    • Simple and planned — Cook at home and make the most of each shop.
    • Everyday favorites — Mostly groceries, with some small treats.
    • A little more choice — Good variety and some convenience foods.
    • ✓ Food I love — Specialty ingredients and more convenience. (selected)
    • No skimping — Premium ingredients and a well-stocked kitchen.
  4. How many dinners out would you like each week?

    Answer: 4–5 dinners a week — Dinner out is a big part of the week.

    • Occasional dinners — Less than 1 dinner out a week.
    • 1 dinner a week — A casual meal out to look forward to.
    • 2–3 dinners a week — Regular casual meals, with a special dinner sometimes.
    • ✓ 4–5 dinners a week — Dinner out is a big part of the week. (selected)
    • 6–7 dinners a week — Most evenings out, including memorable dining.
  5. What kind of travel would you like?

    Answer: A few adventures — Longer trips and weekend escapes.

    • Close to home — Local adventures and day trips.
    • A simple getaway — Save up for a modest trip.
    • An annual escape — A proper trip, with room to enjoy it.
    • ✓ A few adventures — Longer trips and weekend escapes. (selected)
    • Travel in style — Several big trips with extra comfort.
  6. What entertainment would you enjoy?

    Answer: A full calendar — More concerts, tickets, and nights out.

    • Keep it simple — Free events, streaming, and nights with friends.
    • A few nights out — Movies or a small show now and then.
    • Regular plans — Movies, music, and shows through the month.
    • ✓ A full calendar — More concerts, tickets, and nights out. (selected)
    • Make it special — Premium seats and big entertainment experiences.
  7. How would you spend time on hobbies and recreation?

    Answer: Go deeper — More lessons, equipment, and active weekends.

    • Outdoors and free — Parks, walks, and low-cost hobbies.
    • A few favorites — A simple hobby or fitness routine.
    • Time for my interests — Classes, sports, and memberships.
    • ✓ Go deeper — More lessons, equipment, and active weekends. (selected)
    • Big hobbies — Premium clubs, equipment, and recreation.
  8. What feels like your personal style?

    Answer: Style is a priority — Better brands and more frequent updates.

    • Thrift and reuse — Find good pieces and make them last.
    • Everyday basics — Affordable favorites and occasional replacements.
    • A few quality pieces — Everyday brands, with a little room for treats.
    • ✓ Style is a priority — Better brands and more frequent updates. (selected)
    • Designer choices — Premium pieces are part of the picture.
  9. How much room would you like for future goals?

    Answer: Make saving a priority — Set aside a substantial part of life’s budget.

    • Start a cushion — Build a small emergency fund.
    • Keep it steady — Put something aside each month.
    • Build more security — Grow savings for the next chapter.
    • Move toward big goals — Save more for a home, change, or opportunity.
    • ✓ Make saving a priority — Set aside a substantial part of life’s budget. (selected)
